books.section: Topic 6.7 Labor in the Gilded Age

primary_sources: Historical Statistics of the United States, Table Ba4954-4964 (work stoppages, workers involved)

rationales.B: 1886 is the first year the workers column passes 500,000, at 610,000.
rationales.C: 439,000 in 1887 is below 500,000, and 1887 comes after 1886.
rationales.general:
Read down the workers column in order.
1. 1881 through 1884 stay between 130,000 and 170,000.
2. 1885 rises to 258,000, still below half a million.
3. 1886 jumps to 610,000, the first year past 500,000.
4. Later years fall back below it, so 1886 is the first.
Remember: “first” means read the column in order and stop at the first hit.

source: original; stimulus verified against its source (see source_note)
stem: In which year did the number of workers involved in stoppages first pass 500,000?
